title: On a Painter’s Table
description: Look over familiar painting materials, supports, and the small parts of a brush.
cardDescription: Look over familiar painting materials, supports, and the small parts of a brush.
focus: The clues describe what an object holds or does. A whole tool and one of its parts have distinct names.
solvingTip: Look for a support, a color material, or a working tool.
words: Stand supporting a picture while it is painted
Strong fabric surface used for many paintings
Surface on which a painter arranges and mixes colors
Bristled tool used to place paint on a surface
Single stiff hair or fiber forming the working end of a brush
Part of a painting brush held by the artist
Squeezable container holding some artists' paints
Colored material spread onto a picture surface
Protective garment worn over an artist’s clothes
Fabric used for wiping painting equipment
Open container holding water or another working material
Quick preliminary drawing for a picture

answerNotes.EASEL: An easel is the supporting stand. Canvas is the surface held on it.
answerNotes.PALETTE: Palette is the painter’s color surface. Palate and pallet sound similar but have different meanings.
answerNotes.PIGMENT: Pigment supplies color to paint. It differs from the liquid or binder carrying it.
answerNotes.CANVAS: Canvas names the fabric support here. It can also name the finished painting on that support.

title: Around a Color Wheel
description: Explore familiar color names and the words painters use for lighter, darker, and related colors.
cardDescription: Explore familiar color names and the words painters use for lighter, darker, and related colors.
focus: The clues describe visible qualities rather than requiring a color-mixing exercise. Some everyday temperature words have a visual meaning.
solvingTip: Look for a color name, a lightness word, or a way colors are arranged.
words: Warm color associated with ripe strawberries
Color associated with a clear daytime sky
Color associated with many fresh leaves
Color between red and yellow on a traditional paint wheel
Purple color between blue and red on a traditional wheel
Another word for a basic color quality
Color made lighter by adding white in traditional painting usage
Color made darker by adding black in traditional painting usage
Color’s lightness or darkness in one common art use
Color description associated with reds and yellows
Color description associated with blues and many greens

answerNotes.TINT: Tint commonly means a color lightened with white. Shade describes darkening with black in traditional painting terminology.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade is a color term here. It does not mean shelter from direct sunlight.
answerNotes.HUE: Hue identifies a basic color family. It is distinct from how light or dark that color appears.
answerNotes.WHEEL: A color wheel organizes relationships around a circle. It is a diagram rather than a rotating vehicle part.

title: A Watercolor Afternoon
description: Explore watercolor through familiar surfaces, tools, and words describing paint and water.
cardDescription: Explore watercolor through familiar surfaces, tools, and words describing paint and water.
focus: The clues identify visual effects and materials without prescribing a technique. Several short words refer to a condition or action.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a material, a layer, or a surface condition.
words: Painting medium using pigments dispersed with water
Common absorbent support for a watercolor picture
Liquid used to carry watercolor pigment
Tool used to move a watercolor wash onto paper
Broad thin application of diluted paint
Thin transparent painted layer over an earlier layer
One application placed over or beneath another
Boundary where one painted area ends
To join colors with a gradual transition
Containing visible moisture on a painting surface
No longer wet on a painting surface
Bright illumination affecting how a picture is seen
Transparent rather than cloudy in appearance
Small touch made with a brush

answerNotes.WASH: Wash is a thin application of paint here. It does not mean cleaning the finished picture.
answerNotes.GLAZE: A glaze is a transparent layer in this art setting. It is not a sweet food coating.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper is a painting support rather than the paint itself. Different paper surfaces can produce different visual textures.
answerNotes.LAYER: A layer is one application or level. The word describes its position relative to other applications.

title: A Visit to the Art Gallery
description: Browse familiar picture types, display objects, and the words used around a gallery.
cardDescription: Browse familiar picture types, display objects, and the words used around a gallery.
focus: The clues identify art forms and the objects displaying them. The subject of a picture can be as useful as its material.
solvingTip: Look for a picture type, a display part, or a person viewing the work.
words: Border supporting or surrounding a picture
Person creating a painting or other artwork
Name given to a displayed artwork
Small written description beside a gallery work
Upright surface on which a picture hangs
Enclosed display space within a gallery
Brief drawn study displayed as an artwork
Word naming a paint medium using drying oils
Artist paint using a synthetic resin emulsion

answerNotes.PORTRAIT: A portrait focuses on a person or people. A landscape instead focuses on outdoor scenery.
answerNotes.STILLLIFE: Still life is normally written as two words. The grid joins the letters for the picture type.
answerNotes.LABEL: A gallery label supplies written information. It is separate from the artwork’s decorative frame.
answerNotes.LANDSCAPE: Landscape is a picture category here. The clue does not mean turning a page sideways.

title: Objects in a Still Life
description: Look closely at familiar objects and the visual words used when arranging a still-life picture.
cardDescription: Look closely at familiar objects and the visual words used when arranging a still-life picture.
focus: The clues combine everyday things with ways artists describe their appearance. Outline, volume, and surface have distinct terms.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names an object, an outline, or a surface quality. Short object words can help with the visual terms.
words: Rounded tree fruit often arranged in a still-life bowl
Fruit often wider at the base than near its stem
Container holding flowers in a still-life arrangement
Rounded open vessel represented on an artist’s table
Narrow-necked container used as a picture subject
Flat surface supporting a still-life arrangement
Fabric draped beneath objects in a painting
Darkened area where an object blocks light
An object’s three-dimensional shape in art
An outline or flat enclosed area in a picture
Visible path drawn along a picture surface
Line bending gradually rather than running straight
Surface quality suggested or shown in a picture

answerNotes.FORM: Form suggests three-dimensional volume. Shape can describe a flat outline or area.
answerNotes.TEXTURE: Texture concerns surface quality. A painting can suggest a rough or smooth texture without using that physical material.
answerNotes.SHADOW: A shadow is an effect of blocked light. It differs from the object casting it.
answerNotes.LINE: A line is a drawn path here. It does not mean a queue of gallery visitors.
